mathematical_or_operational_scope: Finite-field control of the arbitrary-length two-boundary-defect Fourier identity for a three-character sequence.
positive_controls: Lines 22–23 select exact power-of-two roots for the fixed prime/length pairs; the n/2 test suffices because every selected n is a power of two.
Lines 27–34 independently interpolate three starting values and compare direct Fourier rows with the two defect terms. Output explicitly disclaims factorization.

findings.issue: solve assumes a square nonsingular system over a field and root selection assumes fixed valid primes. Shape, primality and singularity errors are not normalized for general callers.
Finite samples at selected powers of two validate instances, not a universal arbitrary-length theorem. The single identity assertion is removable with optimized Python.

cost_and_scaling: Per trial the direct row sums cost O(n^2) modular arithmetic plus exponentiation; interpolation is a constant 3x3 solve. O(n) working storage. No fast Fourier application or factorization is implemented.
test_scope_and_limits: Designed fixed test set: p in {257,65537}, n in {8,16,32,64,128}, two roots and ten trials. The row counter counts n-3 rows per trial. No test execution in this review.
certificate_acceptance: Checks an identity for constructed control sequences. It never checks a full stage factorization, all corner guards, arbitrary primes, or all lengths.
